co_baldy_overlook.blurb: Baldy Overlook is a newer sandstone crag in the forest above Durango, up on the Missionary Ridge side at roughly 9,000 feet. Of its 29 lines, about 25 are bolted and four are trad. Difficulty is spread fairly evenly from 5.8 through the low 5.12s, with the bulk of the climbing between 5.10 and 5.12. The cliff band faces mostly south and sits right above a field of boulders, though a few lines stay shaded most of the day. The stone is good in places but still being cleaned, so bring a brush. Dry winters are the prime time here; the elevation and breezes keep summer days bearable too.

co_zappa_wall.blurb: Zappa Wall is one of the stronger cliffs in Escalante Canyon, a sandstone canyon outside Grand Junction at around 6,200 feet. Nearly all of its 28 routes are trad, built from cracks, corners and roofs, plus one aid line. Climbing is sustained and steep, a bit like a smaller version of Indian Creek, and the grades center on 5.10 and 5.11 with a few at 5.12 and two at 5.13. The wall catches sun in the morning. Reaching it means a climb up a talus slope, and small plaques at the base give route details, though not every line has one.

co_recovery_wall.blurb: Recovery Wall is a red granite face in the South Platte portion of Devil's Head, at roughly 8,900 feet. Almost all of its 28 routes are bolted, with just two trad lines, and around half of the sport routes are two pitches. The rock is high quality and the climbing runs from crimpy, balancy faces to a wide chimney. Difficulty concentrates in 5.10 to 5.12, with a few easier options from 5.7 to 5.9. The wall points southeast, so it takes sun early and falls into shade by early afternoon, helped by big trees growing in front of it.

co_falls_wall.blurb: Falls Wall stands on the east rim of Castlewood Canyon, a shallow conglomerate canyon on the plains southeast of Denver, near the creek's waterfall. The 28 climbs are a mixed bag: sport, trad and top-rope lines, a few boulder problems and one aid route. The grades lean hard, with the largest group in the 5.11 range, though a few easier climbs and a couple of V-scale problems exist. Walls here are short and steep, and the rock is a coarse, cobbly conglomerate with plenty of open fractures at the rim, so expect to place gear carefully and watch for loose blocks.

co_crag_ranch_the.blurb: The Crag Ranch sits in the newer western valley of Devil's Head, a granite area in the South Platte region southwest of Denver, at about 9,500 feet. Roughly two thirds of the 28 routes are bolted and the rest are trad. Several sport lines are multipitch or very long, and most of the difficulty is in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with some easier options from 5.5 to 5.10. The fine-grained granite is excellent, and the main formation is a roughly 250-foot west-facing wall. A north-facing alcove holds around 15 routes, so shade is easy to find on hot days and sun on cold ones.

co_bastille_w_face_the.blurb: The west face of the Bastille is a historic proving ground in Eldorado Canyon State Park, just outside Boulder. This sandstone wall carries 28 routes, nearly all trad, with two sport lines. Grades run from 5.7 up to a single 5.13, but the heart of it is 5.8 through 5.11, with the most routes at 5.11 and 5.10. The face takes sun through the afternoon, making it a good pick for cooler months. Reach the base by a steep third-class path just around the corner. Plan on loose rock and flexing flakes, and descents that are exposed.
